p2.original: More than Cooking, Heating, and Cooling

p3.original: If you live in the United States, there is a slightly better than 50–50 chance your home is heated and cooled using natural gas. You may even use natural gas for cooking. However, those uses are not the primary uses of natural gas in the U.S. In late 2021, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration, home heating, cooling, and cooking accounted for nearly 20% of natural gas usage. What accounts for the rest? The greatest uses for natural gas are the generation of electric power (almost 37%) and in industry (30%). Together these three uses for natural gas touch many areas of our lives, so why would there be any opposition to a merger of two natural gas firms? After all, a merger could mean increased efficiencies and reduced costs to people like you and me.
p3.zh: 如果你住在美国,你家用天然气加热和冷却的可能性会略高于50-50。 你甚至可以用天然气做饭 然而,这些用途并不是美国天然气的主要用途.2021年末,据美国报道.能源信息管理局、家庭供暖、冷却和烹饪占天然气使用量的近20%。其余的都算什么账?天然气的最大用途是发电(将近37%)和工业(30%)。天然气的这三种用途共同触及我们生活的很多领域,那么为什么有人反对将两家天然气公司合并?毕竟,合并可能意味着提高效率 降低你和我这样的人的成本。

p4.original: In October 2011, Kinder Morgan and El Paso Corporation, two natural gas firms, announced they were merging. The announcement stated the combined firm would link “nearly every major production region with markets,” cut costs by “eliminating duplication in pipelines and other assets,” and that “the savings could be passed on to consumers.”
p4.zh: 2011年10月,Kinder Morgan和El Paso Corporation两家天然气公司宣布合并.公告称,合并公司将“几乎将每个主要生产区与市场挂钩”,通过“消除管道和其他资产的重复”削减成本,并且“节省的资金可以转给消费者”。

p5.original: The objection? The $21.1 billion deal would give Kinder Morgan control of more than 80,000 miles of pipeline, making the new firm the third largest energy producer in North America. Policymakers and the public wondered whether the new conglomerate really would pass on cost savings to consumers, or would the merger give Kinder Morgan a strong oligopoly position in the natural gas marketplace?
p5.zh: 反对?211亿美元的交易将使金德摩根控制超过8万英里的管道,使新公司成为北美第三大能源生产国.决策者和公众想知道,新的企业集团是否真的会把成本节约转移给消费者,还是合并会让Kinder Morgan在天然气市场中处于强大的寡头垄断地位?

p6.original: That brings us to the central questions this chapter poses: What should the balance be between corporate size and a larger number of competitors in a marketplace, and what role should the government play in this balancing act?
p6.zh: 这就让我们想到本章提出的核心问题:公司规模与市场中更多的竞争者之间应如何平衡,政府在这种平衡行为中应发挥什么作用?

p13.original: The previous chapters on the theory of the firm identified three important lessons: First, that competition, by providing consumers with lower prices and a variety of innovative products, is a good thing; second, that large-scale production can dramatically lower average costs; and third, that markets in the real world are rarely perfectly competitive. As a consequence, government policymakers must determine how much to intervene to balance the potential benefits of large-scale production against the potential loss of competition that can occur when businesses grow in size, especially through mergers.
p13.zh: 前几章关于公司理论的论述确定了三个重要教训:第一,通过向消费者提供较低的价格和各种创新产品来进行竞争,是一件好事;第二,大规模生产可以大大降低平均成本;第三,现实世界的市场很少完全具有竞争力. 因此,政府决策者必须确定应进行多少干预,以平衡大规模生产的潜在利益与企业规模扩大,特别是通过兼并扩大而可能发生的竞争损失。

p14.original: For example, in 2006, AT&T and BellSouth proposed a merger. At the time, there were very few mobile phone service providers. Both the Justice Department and the FCC blocked the proposal.
p14.zh: 例如,2006年,AT&T和BellSouth提议合并. 当时,移动电话服务提供商很少。司法部和公平竞争委员会都阻止了这项提案。

p15.original: The two companies argued that the merger would benefit consumers, who would be able to purchase better telecommunications services at a cheaper price because the newly created firm would take advantage of economies of scale and eliminate duplicate investments. However, a number of activist groups like the Consumer Federation of America and Public Knowledge expressed fears that the merger would reduce competition and lead to higher prices for consumers for decades to come. In December 2006, the federal government allowed the merger to proceed. By 2009, the new post-merger AT&T was the eighth largest company by revenues in the United States, and by that measure the largest telecommunications company in the world. Economists have spent – and will still spend – years trying to determine whether the merger of AT&T and BellSouth, as well as other smaller mergers of telecommunications companies at about this same time, helped consumers, hurt them, or did not make much difference.
p15.zh: 这两家公司认为,合并将有利于消费者,消费者能够以更低廉的价格购买更好的电信服务,因为新成立的公司将利用规模经济并消除重复投资。 然而,美国消费者联合会和公共知识等一些活跃团体表示担心,合并将减少竞争,导致消费者在未来几十年中价格上升。2006年12月,联邦政府允许进行合并。 到2009年,新的合并后AT&T是美国收入第八大公司,并以此衡量世界上最大的电信公司.经济学家们花费了 — — 并且仍将花费 — — 几年来试图确定AT&T和Bell South的合并,以及电信公司在大约这一时段的其他较小的合并,是否帮助了消费者,伤害了他们,或者没有产生多大影响。

p16.original: This chapter discusses public policy issues about competition. How can economists and governments determine when mergers of large companies like AT&T and BellSouth should be allowed and when they should be blocked? The government also plays a role in policing anticompetitive behavior other than mergers, like prohibiting certain kinds of contracts that might restrict competition. In the case of natural monopoly, however, trying to preserve competition probably will not work very well, and so government will often resort to regulation of price and/or quantity of output. In recent decades, there has been a global trend toward less government intervention in the price and output decisions of businesses.
p16.zh: 本章讨论有关竞争的公共政策问题。经济学家和政府如何决定何时允许AT&T和Bell South等大公司的合并,何时应阻止它们? 政府还在监管除合并以外的反竞争行为方面发挥作用,例如禁止某些可能限制竞争的合同。 然而,在自然垄断的情况下,试图保持竞争可能不会很好,因此政府往往会诉诸于对价格和/或产出数量的管理。近几十年来,全球的趋势是政府对企业价格和产出决定的干预减少。

p18.original: A corporate merger occurs when two formerly separate firms combine to become a single firm. When one firm purchases another, it is called an acquisition. An acquisition may not look just like a merger, since the newly purchased firm may continue to operate under its former company name. Mergers can also be lateral, where two firms of similar sizes combine to become one. However, both mergers and acquisitions lead to two formerly separate firms operating under common ownership, and so they are commonly grouped together.
p18.zh: 当两个原先独立的公司合并成为一个单一的公司时,就发生了公司合并。 当一家公司购买另一家公司时,它就被称为收购。 由于新购买的公司可能继续以其原公司名称经营,因此收购可能不象合并。兼并也可以是横向的,两家规模类似的公司合并成为一家公司。 然而,兼并和收购都导致两家以前分开的公司在共同所有权下运作,因此它们通常被合并在一起。

p20.original: Since a merger combines two firms into one, it can reduce the extent of competition between firms. Therefore, when two U.S. firms announce a merger or acquisition where at least one of the firms is above a minimum size of sales (a threshold that moves up gradually over time, and was at $101 million in 2022), or certain other conditions are met, they are required under law to notify the U.S. Federal Trade Commission (FTC). The left-hand panel of  (a) shows the number of mergers submitted for review to the FTC each year from 1999 to 2012. Mergers follow the business cycle, falling after the 2001 recession, peaking in 2007 as the Great Recession struck, and then rising since 2009. The right-hand panel of  (b) shows the distribution of those mergers submitted for review in 2015 as measured by the size of the transaction. It is important to remember that this total leaves out many small mergers under $50 million, which companies only need to report in certain limited circumstances. In 2012, 26 percent of all reported merger and acquisition transactions exceeded $500 million, while 11 percent exceeded $1 billion.
p20.zh: 由于合并将两家公司合并为一个公司,因此可以减少公司之间的竞争。 因此,当两家美国公司宣布合并或收购时,至少有一家公司在最低销售规模以上(这一门槛随时间推移而逐步上升,2022年达到1.01亿美元),或者满足某些其他条件时,它们必须依法通知美国。联邦贸易委员会。(a) 左边小组显示1999年至2012年每年提交公平贸易委员会审查的合并案数目。合并遵循商业周期,在2001年衰退后下降,2007年随着大衰退的冲击达到顶峰,然后自2009年上升.(b) 的右侧小组显示根据交易规模衡量的提交2015年审查的合并的分布情况。 必须记住,这一总数中不包括5 000万美元以下的许多小型合并,公司只有在有限的特定情况下才需要报告。2012年,在报告的合并和收购交易中,26%超过5亿美元,11%超过10亿美元。

p22.original: The laws that give government the power to block certain mergers, and even in some cases to break up large firms into smaller ones, are called antitrust laws. Before a large merger happens, the antitrust regulators at the FTC, the FCC, the U.S. Department of Justice, or other regulatory agencies can allow the merger, prohibit it, or allow it if certain conditions are met. One common condition is that the merger will be allowed if the firm agrees to sell off certain parts. For example, in 2006, Johnson & Johnson bought the Pfizer’s “consumer health” division, which included well-known brands like Listerine mouthwash and Sudafed cold medicine. As a condition of allowing the merger, Johnson & Johnson was required to sell off six brands to other firms, including Zantac® heartburn relief medication, Cortizone anti-itch cream, and Balmex diaper rash medication, to preserve a greater degree of competition in these markets.
p22.zh: 赋予政府权力阻止某些兼并,甚至在某些情况下将大公司拆分为较小公司的法律,被称为反托拉斯法. 在大规模合并发生前,FTC,FCC,美国的反托拉斯监管机构.司法部或其他管理机构可以允许合并,禁止合并,或者在某些条件得到满足的情况下允许合并。 一个常见条件是,如果公司同意出售某些部件,将允许合并。 例如,在2006年,Johnson & Johnson购买了辉瑞公司的"消费者健康"分部,其中包括了著名的品牌,如Listerine洗口水和Sudafed冷药. 作为允许合并的一个条件,约翰逊 & 约翰逊被要求将六个品牌出售给其他公司,包括Zantac ⁇ 心痛的救治药,Cortizone抗排泄霜,和Balmex尿布疹药,以保持这些市场的更大程度的竞争.

p23.original: The U.S. government approves most proposed mergers. In a market-oriented economy, firms have the freedom to make their own choices. Private firms generally have the freedom to:
p23.zh: 美国政府批准大部分拟议的兼并. 在市场经济中,公司有作出自己选择的自由。私人公司一般可以自由:

p26.original: open new factories or sales facilities or close them
p26.zh: 开办或关闭新的工厂或销售设施;

p27.original: hire workers or to lay them off

p28.original: start selling new products or stop selling existing ones
p28.zh: 开始销售新产品或停止销售现有产品

p29.original: If the owners want to acquire a firm or be acquired, or to merge with another firm, this decision is just one of many that firms are free to make. In these conditions, the managers of private firms will sometimes make mistakes. They may close down a factory which, it later turns out, would have been profitable. They may start selling a product that ends up losing money. A merger between two companies can sometimes lead to a clash of corporate personalities that makes both firms worse off. However, the fundamental belief behind a market-oriented economy is that firms, not governments, are in the best position to know if their actions will lead to attracting more customers or producing more efficiently.
p29.zh: 如果业主想收购一家公司或被收购,或与另一家公司合并,这一决定只是公司可以自由作出的许多决定之一。 在这种情况下,私营公司的管理人员有时会犯错误。 他们可能关闭一家工厂,后来发现,这家工厂本来是有利可图的。 他们可能开始销售一种最终会失去金钱的产品. 两家公司合并有时会导致公司人物冲突,使两家公司处境更差。 然而,市场经济背后的基本信念是,公司,而不是政府,最能够知道它们的行动是否会吸引更多的客户或更有效地生产。

p30.original: Government regulators agree that most mergers are beneficial to consumers. As the Federal Trade Commission has noted on its website (as of November, 2013): “Most mergers actually benefit competition and consumers by allowing firms to operate more efficiently.” At the same time, the FTC recognizes, “Some [mergers] are likely to lessen competition. That, in turn, can lead to higher prices, reduced availability of goods or services, lower quality of products, and less innovation. Some mergers create a concentrated market, while others enable a single firm to raise prices.” The challenge for the antitrust regulators at the FTC and the U.S. Department of Justice is to figure out when a merger may hinder competition. This decision involves both numerical tools and some judgments that are difficult to quantify. The following Clear It Up explains the origins of U.S. antitrust law.
p30.zh: 政府监管机构一致认为,大多数兼并对消费者有利。 正如联邦贸易委员会在其网站(截至2013年11月)中所指出的,“大多数合并实际上有利于竞争和消费者,允许公司更有效地运作。” 与此同时,公平贸易委员会承认,“有些[合并]有可能减少竞争。 这反过来又会导致价格上涨、商品或服务供应减少、产品质量下降以及创新减少。 有些合并创造了集中市场,而另一些则使一家公司能够提高价格。”司法部将查明合并何时可能妨碍竞争。这一决定既涉及数字工具,也涉及一些难以量化的判决。 以下Clear It Up解释了美国反托拉斯法的起源.

p31.zh: 美国的反托拉斯法是什么?

p32.original: In the closing decades of the 1800s, many industries in the U.S. economy were dominated by a single firm that had most of the sales for the entire country. Supporters of these large firms argued that they could take advantage of economies of scale and careful planning to provide consumers with products at low prices. However, critics pointed out that when competition was reduced, these firms were free to charge more and make permanently higher profits, and that without the goading of competition, it was not clear that they were as efficient or innovative as they could be.
p32.zh: 1800年代最后几十年,美国经济中的许多行业都由一家独资公司主导,为全国拥有大部分的销售额. 这些大公司的支持者认为,他们可以利用规模经济和谨慎的规划,以低价向消费者提供产品。 然而,批评者指出,当竞争减少时,这些公司可以自由收取更多的费用,并永远获得更高的利润,如果没有对竞争的嘲弄,它们是否高效或富有创意并不清楚。

p33.original: In many cases, these large firms were organized in the legal form of a “trust,” in which a group of formerly independent firms were consolidated by mergers and purchases, and a group of “trustees” then ran the companies as if they were a single firm. Thus, when the U.S. government sought to limit the power of these trusts, it passed the  Sherman Antitrust Act in 1890 - the nation's first antitrust law. In an early demonstration of the law’s power, the U.S. Supreme Court in 1911 upheld the government’s right to break up Standard Oil, which had controlled about 90% of the country’s oil refining, into 34 independent firms, including Exxon, Mobil, Amoco, and Chevron. In 1914, the Clayton Antitrust Act outlawed mergers and acquisitions (where the outcome would be to “substantially lessen competition” in an industry), price discrimination (where different customers are charged different prices for the same product), and tied sales (where purchase of one product commits the buyer to purchase some other product). Also in 1914, the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) was created to define more specifically what competition was unfair. In 1950, the Celler-Kefauver Act extended the Clayton Act by restricting vertical and conglomerate mergers.  A vertical merger occurs when two or more firms, operating at different levels within an industry's supply chain, merge operations. A conglomerate merger is a merger between firms that are involved in totally unrelated business activities. In the twenty-first century, the FTC and the U.S. Department of Justice continue to enforce antitrust laws.
p33.zh: 在许多情况下,这些大型公司是以“信托”的法律形式组建的,其中一批原先独立的公司通过合并和购买合并,一批“受托人”然后以单一公司的形式经营公司。 因此,当美国政府试图限制这些信托的权力时,它于1890年通过了"谢尔曼反托拉斯法"——全国第一部反托拉斯法. 在早期展示法律的力量时,美国.最高法院在1911年维护了政府将标准石油公司拆分的权利,因为标准石油公司已经控制了全国约90%的炼油工作,分得34家独立公司,包括埃克森,莫比尔,阿莫科和雪佛龙.1914年,《克莱顿反托拉斯法》宣布合并和收购(其结果是“大幅度降低”某一行业的竞争)、价格歧视(不同的客户对同一产品收取不同的价格)以及附带条件的销售(购买一种产品迫使买方购买其他一些产品)。 同样在1914年,联邦贸易委员会(FTC)成立,更具体地界定什么竞争是不公平的.1950年,"策勒-凯福弗法案"通过限制纵向和联合合并,延长了"克莱顿法案".在一个行业供应链内不同层次经营的两家或多家企业合并业务时,发生纵向兼并.企业集团合并是指参与完全无关的商业活动的公司之间的合并. 在21世纪,FTC和美国.司法部继续执行反托拉斯法。

p35.original: Regulators have struggled for decades to measure the degree of monopoly power in an industry. An early tool was the concentration ratio, which measures the combined market share (or percent of total industry sales) which is accounted for by the largest firms (typically the top four to eight). For an explanation of how high market concentrations can create inefficiencies in an economy, refer to Monopoly.
p35.zh: 监管者几十年来一直在努力衡量一个行业的垄断力量程度。 一个早期的工具是集中比率,它衡量最大的公司(通常为前四至前八家公司)所占市场份额(或占工业总销售额的百分比)。 关于市场高度集中如何造成经济体效率低下的解释,请参见垄断。

p36.original: Say that the market for replacing broken automobile windshields in a certain city has 18 firms with the market shares in  , where the market share is each firm’s proportion of total sales in that market. We calculate the four-firm concentration ratio by adding the market shares of the four largest firms: in this case, 16 + 10 + 8 + 6 = 40. We do not consider this concentration ratio especially high, because the largest four firms have less than half the market.

p52.original: The concentration ratio approach can help to clarify some of the fuzziness over deciding when a merger might affect competition. For instance, if two of the smallest firms in the hypothetical market for repairing automobile windshields merged, the four-firm concentration ratio would not change—which implies that there is not much worry that the degree of competition in the market has notably diminished. However, if the top two firms merged, then the four-firm concentration ratio would become 46 (that is, 26 + 8 + 6 + 6). While this concentration ratio is modestly higher, the four-firm concentration ratio would still be less than half, so such a proposed merger might barely raise an eyebrow among antitrust regulators.
p52.zh: 集中比率办法有助于澄清在决定合并何时可能影响竞争方面有些模糊不清之处。 例如,如果在修理汽车挡风玻璃的假设市场中最小的两家公司合并,四家公司的集中比率就不会改变——这意味着对市场竞争程度明显下降并不十分担心。 但是,如果前两家公司合并,那么四家公司的集中比率将变为46(即26+8+6+6)。 虽然这种集中比率略高,但四公司集中比率仍然不到一半,因此,这种拟议的合并在反托拉斯管理机构中几乎不会引起注意。

p55.original: A four-firm concentration ratio is a simple tool, which may reveal only part of the story. For example, consider two industries that both have a four-firm concentration ratio of 80. However, in one industry five firms each control 20% of the market, while in the other industry, the top firm holds 77% of the market and all the other firms have 1% each. Although the four-firm concentration ratios are identical, it would be reasonable to worry more about the extent of competition in the second case—where the largest firm is nearly a monopoly—than in the first.
p55.zh: 四体集中比率是一个简单的工具,可能只揭示故事的一部分. 例如,考虑两个行业,这两个行业的四公司集中比率为80。 然而,在一个行业,5家公司各控制20%的市场,而在另一个行业,顶级公司占有77%的市场,所有其他公司各占1%。 虽然四家公司的集中比率相同,但较之第一公司,在第二起案件中最大的公司几乎是垄断公司,更担心竞争的程度是合理的。

p56.original: Another approach to measuring industry concentration that can distinguish between these two cases is called the Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI). We calculate HHI by summing the squares of the market share of each firm in the industry, as the following Work It Out shows.
p56.zh: 另一种可以区分这两个案例的测量行业集中度的方法是赫芬达尔-赫尔施曼指数(HHI). 我们计算HHI的方法是 将行业中每个公司的市场份额 的平方进行组合,如下文所示。

p58.original: Step 1. Calculate the HHI for a monopoly with a market share of 100%. Because there is only one firm, it has 100% market share. The HHI is 1002 = 10,000.
p58.zh: 步骤1。计算HHI的垄断,市场份额为100%. 因为只有一个公司,它拥有100%的市场份额。HHI为1002=10,000.

p59.original: Step 2. For an extremely competitive industry, with dozens or hundreds of extremely small competitors, the  HHI value might drop as low as 100 or even less. Calculate the HHI for an industry with 100 firms that each have 1% of the market. In this case, the HHI is 100(12) = 100.
p59.zh: 步骤二. 对于竞争激烈的行业,拥有数十或数百个极小的竞争对手,HHI值可能下降至100甚至更低。计算一个行业的HHI,该行业有100家公司,各占市场份额的1%。 在这种情况下,HHI为100(12)=100.

p60.original: Step 3. Calculate the HHI for the industry in . In this case, the HHI is 162 + 102 + 82 + 7(62) + 8(32) = 744.

p61.original: Step 4. Note that the HHI gives greater weight to large firms.

p62.original: Step 5. Consider the earlier example, comparing one industry where five firms each have 20% of the market with an industry where one firm has 77% and the other 23 firms have 1% each. The two industries have the same four-firm concentration ratio of 80. However, the HHI for the first industry is 5(202) = 2,000, while the HHI for the second industry is much higher at 772 + 23(12) = 5,952.
p62.zh: 步骤5。比较一下早先的例子,一个行业,即五家公司各占市场20%,而一个行业,即一家公司占77%,另外23家公司各占1%。 两个行业的四公司集中率相同,为80. 然而,第一产业的HHI为5(202)=2000,而第二产业的HHI为772+23(12)=5,952.

p63.original: Step 6. Note that the near-monopolist in the second industry drives up the HHI measure of industrial concentration.
p63.zh: 步骤6。请注意,第二产业的近乎垄断主义者推动了工业集中的HHI度量.

p93.original: In the 1980s, the FTC followed these guidelines: If a merger would result in an HHI of less than 1,000, the FTC would probably approve it. If a merger would result in an HHI of more than 1,800, the FTC would probably challenge it. If a merger would result in an HHI between 1,000 and 1,800, then the FTC would scrutinize the plan and make a case-by-case decision. However, in the last several decades, the antitrust enforcement authorities have moved away from relying as heavily on measures of concentration ratios and HHIs to determine whether they will allow a merger, and instead they carry out more case-by-case analysis on the extent of competition in different industries.
p93.zh: 1980年代,公平贸易委员会遵循了这些指南:如果合并会导致高健康指数低于1,000,则公平贸易委员会可能批准。 如果合并将导致1,800多HI, 公平贸易委员会可能对此提出质疑。 如果合并将导致1,000至1,800人的健康指数,则公平贸易委员会将仔细审查计划,并逐个作出决定。 然而,在过去几十年里,反托拉斯执法当局不再像依赖集中比率和HHI的衡量标准那样,而是决定它们是否允许合并,而是对不同行业的竞争程度进行更多的逐案分析。

p95.original: Both the four-firm concentration ratio and the Herfindahl-Hirschman index share some weaknesses. First, they begin from the assumption that the “market” under discussion is well-defined, and the only question is measuring how sales are divided in that market. Second, they are based on an implicit assumption that competitive conditions across industries are similar enough that a broad measure of concentration in the market is enough to make a decision about the effects of a merger. These assumptions, however, are not always correct. In response to these two problems, the antitrust regulators have been changing their approach in the last decade or two.
p95.zh: 四公司集中比率和赫芬达尔-赫尔施曼指数都存在一些弱点。 首先,它们首先假定所讨论的“市场”定义明确,唯一的问题是衡量销售在该市场中如何划分。 第二,它们基于一种隐含的假设,即各行业之间的竞争条件十分相似,因此市场中广泛集中的尺度足以就合并的影响作出决定。 然而,这些假设并不总是正确的。 为了应对这两个问题,反托拉斯管理机构在过去十年或两年期间一直在改变做法。

p96.original: Defining a market is often controversial. For example, Microsoft in the early 2000s had a dominant share of the software for computer operating systems. However, in the total market for all computer software and services, including everything from games to scientific programs, the Microsoft share was only about 14% in 2014. A narrowly defined market will tend to make concentration appear higher, while a broadly defined market will tend to make it appear smaller.
p96.zh: 界定市场常常引起争议。 例如,在2000年代初期,微软在计算机操作系统的软件中占有主导份额. 然而,在所有计算机软件和服务的总市场中,包括从游戏到科学程序的一切,微软的股权在2014年只有14%左右.狭义的市场往往会使集中程度显得更高,而广义的市场则往往使它显得较小。

p97.original: In recent decades, there have been two especially important shifts affecting how we define markets: one centers on technology and the other centers on globalization. In addition, these two shifts are interconnected. With the vast improvement in communications technologies, including the development of the internet, a consumer can order books or pet supplies from all over the country or the world. As a result, the degree of competition many local retail businesses face has increased. The same effect may operate even more strongly in markets for business supplies, where so-called “business-to-business” websites can allow buyers and suppliers from anywhere in the world to find each other.
p97.zh: 近几十年来,发生了两个影响我们如何界定市场的特别重要的变化:一个是技术中心,另一个是全球化中心。 此外,这两个转变是相互联系的。 随着通讯技术的巨大改进,包括互联网的发展,消费者可以订购来自全国或全世界的书籍或宠物用品. 因此,许多当地零售企业面临的竞争程度提高了。 在商业用品市场上,同样的效果可能更为强烈,在市场上,所谓的“企业对企业”网站可以使来自世界任何地方的买方和供应商找到对方。

p98.original: Globalization has changed the market boundaries. As recently as the 1970s, it was common for measurements of concentration ratios and HHIs to stop at national borders. Now, many industries find that their competition comes from the global market. A few decades ago, three companies, General Motors, Ford, and Chrysler, dominated the U.S. auto market. By 2014, however, production of these three firms accounted for less than half of U.S. auto sales, although by 2021, with the emergence of COVID-19, the three firms accounted for essentially half of U.S. auto sales. The three firms face competition from well-known car manufacturers such as Toyota, Honda, Nissan, Volkswagen, Mitsubishi, and Mazda. When analysts calculate HHIs with a global perspective, concentration in most major industries—including cars—is lower than in a purely domestic context.
p98.zh: 全球化改变了市场界限。 最近,在1970年代,测量浓度比率和高健康指数时通常会停留在国界。 现在,许多行业发现它们的竞争来自于全球市场.几十年前,通用汽车公司,福特公司,克莱斯勒公司三家公司主导了美国汽车市场. 然而,到2014年,这三家公司的生产量只占美国汽车销售量的一半以下,尽管到2021年,随着COVID-19的出现,这三家公司基本上占美国汽车销售量的一半. 三家公司面临丰田,本田,尼山,大众,三菱,马兹达等著名汽车制造商的竞争. 当分析人员从全球角度计算HHI时,大多数主要工业(包括汽车)的集中程度低于纯粹的国内背景。

p99.original: Because attempting to define a particular market can be difficult and controversial, the Federal Trade Commission has begun to look less at market share and more at the data on actual competition between businesses. For example, in February 2007, Whole Foods Market and Wild Oats Market announced that they wished to merge. These were the two largest companies in the market that the government defined as “premium natural and organic supermarket chains.” However, one could also argue that they were two relatively small companies in the broader market for all stores that sell groceries or specialty food products.
p99.zh: 由于试图定义特定市场可能很困难和有争议,联邦贸易委员会开始少看市场份额,多看企业之间实际竞争的数据. 例如,2007年2月,全美食品市场和野燕市场宣布希望合并. 这些公司是政府定义为“天然和有机超市超级市场”的市场上最大的两家公司。 但是,人们也可以认为,它们只是整个市场中销售食品或食品特产的两家相对较小的公司。

p100.original: Rather than relying on a market definition, the government antitrust regulators looked at detailed evidence on profits and prices for specific stores in different cities, both before and after other competitive stores entered or exited. Based on that evidence, the Federal Trade Commission decided to block the merger. After two years of legal battles, the FTC eventually allowed the merger in 2009 under the conditions that Whole Foods sell off the Wild Oats brand name and a number of individual stores, to preserve competition in certain local markets. For more on the difficulties of defining markets, refer to Monopoly.
p100.zh: 政府反托拉斯监管机构没有依赖市场定义,而是在进入或退出其他竞争性商店之前和之后,仔细研究不同城市具体商店的利润和价格。 根据这一证据,联邦贸易委员会决定阻止合并。 经过两年的法律斗争,FTC最终在2009年允许合并,条件是"全美食品"出售了"野燕"品牌和一些个别商店,以维护某些当地市场的竞争.更多关于界定市场的困难,请参见"垄断".

p101.original: This new approach to antitrust regulation involves detailed analysis of specific markets and companies, instead of defining a market and counting up total sales. A common starting point is for antitrust regulators to use statistical tools and real-world evidence to estimate the demand curves and supply curves the firms proposing a merger face. A second step is to specify how competition occurs in this specific industry. Some possibilities include competing to cut prices, to raise output, to build a brand name through advertising, and to build a reputation for good service or high quality. With these pieces of the puzzle in place, it is then possible to build a statistical model that estimates the likely outcome for consumers if the two firms are allowed to merge. These models do require some degree of subjective judgment, and so they can become the subject of legal disputes between the antitrust authorities and the companies that wish to merge.
p101.zh: 这种新的反托拉斯管制办法涉及对具体市场和公司的详细分析,而不是界定市场和计算总销售额。 一个共同的出发点是,反托拉斯管理机构利用统计工具和现实世界的证据来估计提出兼并面貌的公司的需求曲线和供应曲线。 第二步是具体说明这一具体行业如何发生竞争。 一些可能性包括竞争降低价格,提高产出,通过广告打造品牌,以及建立良好服务或高质量声誉.有了这些拼图,就有可能建立一个统计模型,估计如果允许两家公司合并,消费者可能产生的结果。 这些模式确实需要一定程度的主观判断,因此它们可以成为反托拉斯当局与希望合并的公司之间的法律纠纷的主体.

p103.original: A corporate merger involves two private firms joining together. An acquisition refers to one firm buying another firm. In either case, two formerly independent firms become one firm. Antitrust laws seek to ensure active competition in markets, sometimes by preventing large firms from forming through mergers and acquisitions, sometimes by regulating business practices that might restrict competition, and sometimes by breaking up large firms into smaller competitors.
p103.zh: 公司合并涉及两家私营公司合并。收购是指一家公司收购另一家公司。 在这两种情况下,两家以前独立的公司都成为一家公司。反托拉斯法力求确保市场上的积极竞争,有时是阻止大公司通过合并和收购形成,有时是规范可能限制竞争的商业做法,有时是将大公司拆分为较小的竞争对手。

p104.original: A four-firm concentration ratio is one way of measuring the extent of competition in a market. We calculate it by adding the market shares—that is, the percentage of total sales—of the four largest firms in the market. A Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI) is another way of measuring the extent of competition in a market. We calculate it by taking the market shares of all firms in the market, squaring them, and then summing the total.
p104.zh: 四公司集中比率是衡量市场竞争程度的一种方法。 我们通过增加市场份额来计算,即占市场四大公司销售总额的百分比。赫芬达尔-赫尔施曼指数(HHI)是衡量市场竞争程度的另一种方法. 我们用市场所有企业的市场份额来计算, 盘根错节,然后总结一下总额。

p105.original: The forces of globalization and new communications and information technology have increased the level of competition that many firms face by increasing the amount of competition from other regions and countries.
p105.zh: 全球化和新的通信和信息技术的力量增加了来自其他区域和国家的竞争,提高了许多公司面临的竞争水平。

p107.original:
Is it true that a merger between two firms that are not already in the top four by size can affect both the four-firm concentration ratio and the Herfindahl-Hirschman Index?
Explain briefly.
p107.zh: 规模尚未排在前四的两家公司之间的合并是否确实会影响到四家公司的集中比率和赫芬达尔-赫尔施曼指数?简单解释一下

p108.original: Yes, it is true. The HHI example is easy enough: since the market shares of all firms are included in the HHI calculation, a merger between two of the firms will change the HHI. For the four-firm concentration ratio, it is quite possible that a merger between, say, the fifth and sixth largest firms in the market could create a new firm that is then ranked in the top four in the market. In this case, a merger of two firms, neither in the top four, would still change the four-firm concentration ratio.
p108.zh: 是的,这是真的。HHI的例子很简单:由于所有公司的市场份额都包含在HHI计算中,其中两家公司的合并将改变HHI. 就四公司集中比率而言,市场第五大公司和第六大公司之间的合并,很可能会建立一个新的公司,然后在市场上排名前四。 在这种情况下,两家公司的合并,无论是前四家公司,仍然会改变四家公司的集中比率。

p109.original: Is it true that the four-firm concentration ratio puts more emphasis on one or two very large firms, while the Herfindahl-Hirschman Index puts more emphasis on all the firms in the entire market? Explain briefly.
p109.zh: 四公司集中比率是否确实更强调一两个非常大的公司,而赫芬达尔-赫尔施曼指数则更强调整个市场的所有公司?简单解释一下

p110.original: No, it is not true. The HHI includes the market shares of all firms in its calculation, but the squaring of the market shares has the effect of making the impact of the largest firms relatively bigger than in the 4-firm or 8-firm ratio.
p110.zh: 不,这不是真的HHI在计算时包括所有公司的市场份额,但市场份额的积聚作用是使最大的公司的影响比4公司或8公司的比例大。

p111.original: Some years ago, two intercity bus companies, Greyhound Lines, Inc. and Trailways Transportation System, wanted to merge. One possible definition of the market in this case was “the market for intercity bus service.” Another possible definition was “the market for intercity transportation, including personal cars, car rentals, passenger trains, and commuter air flights.” Which definition do you think the bus companies preferred, and why?
p111.zh: 几年前,两家城际巴士公司灰狗线公司和拖车运输系统希望合并. 这一情况下市场的一个可能的定义是“城际巴士服务市场 ” 。 另一个可能的定义是“城际运输市场,包括个人汽车、汽车租赁、旅客列车和通勤航班 ” 。 你认为巴士公司喜欢哪一个定义,为什么?

p112.original: The bus companies wanted the broader market definition (i.e., the second definition). If the narrow definition had been used, the combined bus companies would have had a near-monopoly on the market for intercity bus service. But they had only a sliver of the market for intercity transportation when everything else was included. The merger was allowed.
p112.zh: 巴士公司希望得到更广泛的市场定义(即第二个定义). 如果采用狭义的定义,联合公交公司在城际公交服务市场上就会出现近乎垄断的情况.但他们只有城际运输市场的一个支架 当其他东西都包括在内时合并获准.

p113.original: As a result of globalization and new information and communications technology, would you expect that the definitions of markets that antitrust authorities use will become broader or narrower?
p113.zh: 由于全球化和新的信息和通信技术,你是否期望反托拉斯当局使用的市场定义将变得更广泛或狭窄?

p114.original: The common expectation is that the definition of markets will become broader because of greater competition from faraway places. However, this broadening doesn’t necessarily mean that antitrust authorities can relax. There is also a fear that companies with a local or national monopoly may use the new opportunities to extend their reach across national borders, and that it will be difficult for national authorities to respond.
p114.zh: 共同的期望是,由于来自遥远地方的竞争加剧,市场的定义将变得更加宽泛。 但这种扩大并不一定意味着反托拉斯当局可以放松。 人们还担心,拥有地方或国家垄断权的公司可能利用新的机会,跨越国界,国家当局难以作出反应。

p150.original: The U.S. antitrust laws reach beyond blocking mergers that would reduce competition to include a wide array of anticompetitive practices. For example, it is illegal for competitors to form a cartel to collude to make pricing and output decisions, as if they were a monopoly firm. The Federal Trade Commission and the U.S. Department of Justice prohibit firms from agreeing to fix prices or output, rigging bids, or sharing or dividing markets by allocating customers, suppliers, territories, or lines of commerce.
p150.zh: 美国的反托拉斯法超越了阻止兼并的范围,这种兼并将减少竞争,包括一系列广泛的反竞争做法。 例如,竞争者组成卡特尔串通作价和产出决定是非法的,似乎他们是一个垄断公司。联邦贸易委员会和美国.司法部禁止公司同意确定价格或产出、操纵投标,或通过分配客户、供应商、领土或商业线路分享或分割市场。

p151.original: In the late 1990s, for example, the antitrust regulators prosecuted an international cartel of vitamin manufacturers, including the Swiss firm Hoffmann-La Roche, the German firm BASF, and the French firm Rhone-Poulenc. These firms reached agreements on how much to produce, how much to charge, and which firm would sell to which customers. Firms like General Mills, Kellogg, Purina Mills, and Procter and Gamble bought the high-priced vitamins, which pushed up the prices more. Hoffmann-La Roche pleaded guilty in May 1999 and agreed both to pay a fine of $500 million and to have at least one top executive be incarcerated for four months.
p151.zh: 例如,1990年代末,反托拉斯监管机构起诉了一个维生素制造商的国际卡特尔,其中包括瑞士Hoffmann-La Roche公司、德国BASF公司和法国Rhone-Poulenc公司。 这些公司就生产多少、收取多少以及哪家公司将向哪家客户出售等问题达成了协议。Mills将军、Kellogg、Purina Mills、Procter和Gamble等公司购买了高价维他命,这促使价格上升。霍夫曼-拉罗什于1999年5月认罪,并同意支付5亿美元的罚款,并至少监禁一名高级行政人员四个月。

p152.original: Under U.S. antitrust laws, monopoly itself is not illegal. If a firm has a monopoly because of a newly patented invention, for example, the law explicitly allows a firm to earn higher-than-normal profits for a time as a reward for innovation. If a firm achieves a large share of the market by producing a better product at a lower price, such behavior is not prohibited by antitrust law.
p152.zh: 根据美国反托拉斯法,垄断本身并不违法. 例如,如果一家公司由于新获得专利的发明而垄断,法律明确允许一家公司在一段时间内赚取高于正常的利润,作为对创新的奖励。 如果一家公司通过低价生产更好的产品,实现了市场的一大份额,那么反托拉斯法并不禁止这种行为.

p154.original: Antitrust law includes rules against restrictive practices—practices that do not involve outright agreements to raise price or to reduce the quantity produced, but that might have the effect of reducing competition. Antitrust cases involving restrictive practices are often controversial, because they delve into specific contracts or agreements between firms that are allowed in some cases but not in others.
p154.zh: 反托拉斯法包括禁止限制性做法的规则——这种做法不涉及直接协议提高价格或减少生产的数量,但可能具有减少竞争的效果。涉及限制性做法的反托拉斯案件往往引起争议,因为它们深入探讨某些情况下允许但另一些情况下不允许的具体合同或公司之间的协议。

p155.original: For example, an exclusive dealing agreement between a manufacturer and a dealer can be legal or illegal. It is legal if the purpose of the contract is to encourage competition between dealers. For example, it is legal for the Ford Motor Company to sell its cars to only Ford dealers, and for General Motors to sell to only GM dealers, and so on. However, exclusive deals may also limit competition. If one large retailer obtained the exclusive rights to be the sole distributor of televisions, computers, and audio equipment made by a number of companies, then this exclusive contract would have an anticompetitive effect on other retailers.
p155.zh: 例如,制造商与经销商之间的排他性交易协议可以是合法或非法的。 如果合同的目的是鼓励经销商之间的竞争,则合同是合法的。 例如,福特汽车公司将其汽车出售给仅福特经销商是合法的,通用汽车公司只出售给GM经销商也是合法的,等等. 然而,独家交易也可能限制竞争。 如果有一个大型零售商获得独家经营一些公司制造的电视、计算机和音频设备,那么这一独家经营合同将对其他零售商产生反竞争影响。

p156.original: Tying sales happen when a customer is allowed to buy one product only if the customer also buys a second product. Tying sales are controversial because they force consumers to purchase a product that they may not actually want or need. Further, the additional, required products are not necessarily advantageous to the customer. Suppose that to purchase a popular DVD, the store required that you also purchase a certain portable TV model. These products are only loosely related, thus there is no reason to make the purchase of one contingent on the other. Even if a customer were interested in a portable TV, the tying to a particular model prevents the customer from having the option of selecting one from the numerous types available in the market.
p156.zh: 附带条件的销售发生于只有在客户也购买了第二种产品的情况下才允许客户购买一种产品.绑定销售有争议,因为其迫使消费者购买他们实际上可能不想要或不需要的产品. 此外,所需额外产品不一定对客户有利。 假如要买一个流行的DVD, 商店要求你也购买一个 某些便携式电视模型。 这些产品只是关系松散,因此没有理由将购买一种产品作为购买另一产品的条件。 即使客户对便携式电视感兴趣,与某一特定型号的捆绑也使客户无法从市场上现有的多种类型中选择一台。

p157.original: A related, but not identical, concept is bundling, where a firm sells two or more products as one. Bundling typically offers an advantage for consumers by allowing them to acquire multiple products or services for a better price. For example, several cable companies allow customers to buy products like cable, internet, and a phone line through a special price available through bundling. Customers are also welcome to purchase these products separately, but the price of bundling is usually more appealing.
p157.zh: 一个相关但并非完全相同的概念是捆绑,即一家公司将两个或两个以上产品作为一个产品出售。邦德灵通常通过允许消费者以更好的价格获得多种产品或服务而为消费者提供优势. 例如,几家有线电视公司允许客户通过捆绑获得特别价格购买有线电视、互联网和电话线路等产品。也欢迎客户单独购买这些产品,但捆绑的价格通常更具吸引力。

p158.original: In some cases, we can view tying sales and bundling as anticompetitive. However, in other cases they may be legal and even common. It is common for people to purchase season tickets to a sports team or a set of concerts so as to guarantee tickets to the few contests or shows that are most popular and likely to sell out. Computer software manufacturers may often bundle a number of different programs, even when the buyer wants only a few. Think about the software that is included in a new computer purchase, for example.
p158.zh: 在某些情况下,我们可以将捆绑销售和捆绑视为反竞争。 但是,在其他情况下,这些可能是合法的,甚至常见的。 人们通常会购买体育队或一套音乐会的赛季门票,以保证参加少数最受欢迎和可能销量较大的比赛或节目的门票.计算机软件制造商可能经常捆绑一些不同的程序,即使买家只想要几个程序. 例如,考虑一下新计算机购买中包含的软件。

p159.original: Recall from the chapter on Monopoly that predatory pricing occurs when the existing firm (or firms) reacts to a new firm by dropping prices very low, until the new firm is driven out of the market, at which point the existing firm raises prices again. This pattern of pricing is aimed at deterring new firms from entering the market. However, in practice, it can be hard to figure out when pricing is predatory. Say that American Airlines is flying between two cities, and a new airline starts flying between the same two cities, at a lower price. If American Airlines cuts its price to match the new entrant, is this predatory pricing or is it just market competition at work? A commonly proposed rule is that if a firm is selling for less than its average variable cost—that is, at a price where it should be shutting down—then there is evidence for predatory pricing. However, calculating in the real world what costs are variable and what costs are fixed is often not obvious, either.
p159.zh: 从关于垄断的一章中回顾,当现有公司(或几家公司)对一家新公司作出反应时,就会出现掠夺性定价,其方式是降低价格,直到新公司被赶出市场,此时,现有公司又提高了价格。 这种定价模式旨在阻止新公司进入市场。 然而,在实践中,价格何时是掠夺性的,可能很难确定。说美国航空在两个城市之间飞行,一个新的航空公司开始在同一两个城市之间飞行,价格较低. 如果美国航空公司削减价格以适应新的进取点,那么这种掠夺性定价是还是只是市场竞争呢?一项普遍提出的规则是,如果一家公司出售的价格低于其平均可变成本,即以应当关闭的价格出售,则有证据表明存在掠夺性定价。 然而,在现实世界中,计算哪些成本是可变的,哪些成本是固定的,也往往不明显。

p160.original: The Microsoft antitrust case embodies many of these gray areas in restrictive practices, as the next Clear It Up shows.
p160.zh: 微软反托拉斯案在限制性做法中体现了许多这些灰色领域,下一部Clear It Up就表明了这一点。

p161.original: Did Microsoft® engage in anticompetitive and restrictive practices?
p161.zh: 微软公司是否从事反竞争和限制性做法?

p162.original: The most famous restrictive practices case of recent years was a series of lawsuits by the U.S. government against Microsoft—lawsuits that some of Microsoft’s competitors encouraged. All sides admitted that Microsoft’s Windows program had a near-monopoly position in the market for the software used in general computer operating systems. All sides agreed that the software had many satisfied customers and that the computer software capabilities were compatible with Windows. Software that Microsoft and other companies produced had expanded dramatically in the 1990s. Having a monopoly or a near-monopoly is not necessarily illegal in and of itself, but in cases where one company controls a great deal of the market, antitrust regulators look at any allegations of restrictive practices with special care.
p162.zh: 近年来最著名的限制性做法案件是美国政府针对微软的法律诉讼,一些微软的竞争者鼓励这些诉讼。各方都承认微软的Windows程序在一般计算机操作系统所使用的软件的市场上占有近乎垄断的地位.各方一致认为,该软件有许多满意的客户,计算机软件能力与Windows兼容.微软和其他公司生产的软件在1990年代大幅扩张.垄断或接近垄断本身不一定是非法的,但当一家公司控制着大量的市场时,反托拉斯管理机构要特别小心地审查关于限制性做法的任何指控。

p163.original: The antitrust regulators argued that Microsoft had gone beyond profiting from its software innovations and its dominant position in the software market for operating systems, and had tried to use its market power in operating systems software to take over other parts of the software industry. For example, the government argued that Microsoft had engaged in an anticompetitive form of exclusive dealing by threatening computer makers that, if they did not leave another firm’s software off their machines (specifically, Netscape’s Internet browser), then Microsoft would not sell them its operating system software. Government antitrust regulators accused Microsoft of tying together its Windows operating system software, where it had a monopoly, with its Internet Explorer browser software, where it did not have a monopoly, and thus using this bundling as an anticompetitive tool. The government also accused Microsoft of a form of predatory pricing; namely, giving away certain additional software products for free as part of Windows, as a way of driving out the competition from other software makers.
p163.zh: 反托拉斯监管机构认为,微软已经超越了从软件创新和在操作系统软件市场中的支配地位中获利,并试图利用其在操作系统软件中的市场力量来接管软件行业的其他部分. 例如,政府辩称微软通过威胁计算机制造者从事一种反竞争的独家交易,如果他们不把另一家公司的软件从他们的机器上离开(具体来说是Netscape的互联网浏览器),微软就不会将它的操作系统软件出售给它们。 政府反托拉斯监管者指责微软将其Windows操作系统软件与互联网探索器浏览器软件捆绑在一起,因为微软在Windows操作系统软件上拥有垄断权,而互联网探索器浏览器软件上并没有垄断权,因此将这种捆绑作为反竞争工具. 政府也指责微软有某种掠夺性定价形式;即作为Windows的一部分,将某些额外的软件产品无偿赠与,以此驱使其他软件制造商的竞争.

p164.original: In April 2000, a federal court held that Microsoft’s behavior had crossed the line into unfair competition, and recommended that the company be split into two competing firms. However, the court overturned that penalty on appeal, and in November 2002 Microsoft reached a settlement with the government that it would end its restrictive practices.
p164.zh: 2000年4月,一家联邦法院认为微软的行为已经越线进入不公平竞争,建议将公司拆分为两家竞争的公司. 然而,法院在上诉时推翻了这一处罚,2002年11月,微软与政府达成和解,将终止其限制性做法.

p165.original: The concept of restrictive practices is continually evolving, as firms seek new ways to earn profits and government regulators define what is permissible. A situation where the law is evolving and changing is always somewhat troublesome, since laws are most useful and fair when firms know what they are in advance. In addition, since the law is open to interpretation, competitors who are losing out in the market can accuse successful firms of anticompetitive restrictive practices, and try to win through government regulation what they have failed to accomplish in the market. Officials at the Federal Trade Commission and the Department of Justice are, of course, aware of these issues, but there is no easy way to resolve them.
p165.zh: 限制性做法的概念在不断演变,因为公司寻求新的盈利方式,而政府监管者则界定了允许的内容。法律正在演变和变化的情况总是有些麻烦,因为当公司事先知道法律是什么时,法律最有用和最公平。 此外,由于法律可以解释,在市场上输掉的竞争者可以指责成功的公司采取反竞争的限制性做法,并试图通过政府监管赢得它们在市场上未能实现的成就。联邦贸易委员会和司法部的官员当然都意识到这些问题,但并不容易解决这些问题。

p167.original: Antitrust authorities block firms from openly colluding to form a cartel that will reduce output and raise prices. Companies sometimes attempt to find other ways around these restrictions and, consequently, many antitrust cases involve restrictive practices that can reduce competition in certain circumstances, like tie-in sales, bundling, and predatory pricing.
p167.zh: 反托拉斯当局阻止各公司公开串通,形成一个将减少产出和抬高价格的卡特尔。公司有时试图绕过这些限制寻找其他办法,因此,许多反托拉斯案件涉及限制性做法,在某些情况下可以减少竞争,如捆绑销售、捆绑和掠夺性定价。

p169.original: Why would a firm choose to use one or more of the anticompetitive practices described in Regulating Anticompetitive Behavior?
p169.zh: 公司为什么选择采用《反竞争行为管理》中描述的一项或多项反竞争做法?

p170.original: Because outright collusion to raise profits is illegal and because existing regulations include gray areas which firms may be able to exploit.
p170.zh: 因为为谋取利润而进行的直接勾结是非法的,而且因为现行条例包括了公司可能加以利用的灰色区域。

p172.original: What is a minimum resale price maintenance agreement? How might it reduce competition and when might it be acceptable?
p172.zh: 什么是最低转售价格维持协议?如何减少竞争以及何时可以接受?

p173.original: What is exclusive dealing? How might it reduce competition and when might it be acceptable?
p173.zh: 什么是独家交易?如何减少竞争以及何时可以接受?

p174.original: What is a tie-in sale? How might it reduce competition and when might it be acceptable?
p174.zh: 什么是捆绑买卖?如何减少竞争以及何时可以接受?

p175.original: What is predatory pricing? How might it reduce competition, and why might it be difficult to tell when it should be illegal?
p175.zh: 掠夺性定价是什么?如何能减少竞争,为何很难知道何时才是非法的?

p177.original: Can you think of any examples of successful predatory pricing in the real world?
p177.zh: 你能想到现实世界中任何掠夺性定价成功的事例吗?

p178.original: If you were developing a product (like a web browser) for a market with significant barriers to entry, how would you try to get your product into the market successfully?
p178.zh: 如果你正在开发一个产品(像网页浏览器),用于一个存在重大进入障碍的市场,你将如何试图成功地将你的产品带入市场?

p180.original: Most true monopolies today in the U.S. are regulated, natural monopolies. A natural monopoly poses a difficult challenge for competition policy, because the structure of costs and demand makes competition unlikely or costly. A natural monopoly arises when average costs are declining over the range of production that satisfies market demand. This typically happens when fixed costs are large relative to variable costs. As a result, one firm is able to supply the total quantity demanded in the market at lower cost than two or more firms—so splitting up the natural monopoly would raise the average cost of production and force customers to pay more.
p180.zh: 今天在美国,大多数真正的垄断都是受管制的,自然的垄断.自然垄断对竞争政策提出了困难的挑战,因为成本和需求的结构使得竞争不太可能或代价高昂。 当平均成本在满足市场需求的生产范围上下降时,自然垄断就会出现。 这通常发生在固定成本相对于可变成本而言是很大的时期。 因此,一家公司能够以低于两家或两家以上公司的价格提供市场所需的总量——因此,将自然垄断分开将提高生产的平均成本,迫使客户支付更多的费用。

p181.original: Public utilities, the companies that have traditionally provided water and electrical service across much of the United States, are leading examples of natural monopoly. It would make little sense to argue that a local water company should be divided into several competing companies, each with its own separate set of pipes and water supplies. Installing four or five identical sets of pipes under a city, one for each water company, so that each household could choose its own water provider, would be terribly costly. The same argument applies to the idea of having many competing companies for delivering electricity to homes, each with its own set of wires. Before the advent of wireless phones, the argument also applied to the idea of many different phone companies, each with its own set of phone wires running through the neighborhood.
p181.zh: 公用事业是美国大部分地区传统上提供水电服务的公司,是自然垄断的主要例子。认为一个当地供水公司应该分成几个相互竞争的公司,每个公司都有自己的一套单独的管道和供水设施,这是没有道理的。在一个城市下安装四、五套相同的管道,每个供水公司各安装一套,这样每个家庭就可以选择自己的供水者,费用将非常昂贵。 同样的论点也适用于让许多竞争的公司为家庭供电的想法,每个公司都有自己的一套电线。 在无线电话出现之前,这一论点也适用于许多不同的电话公司的想法,每个公司都有自己的一套电话线贯穿周边.

p182.original: The Choices in Regulating a Natural Monopoly

p183.original: What then is the appropriate competition policy for a natural monopoly?  illustrates the case of natural monopoly, with a market demand curve that cuts through the downward-sloping portion of the average cost curve. Points A, B, C, and F illustrate four of the main choices for regulation.  outlines the regulatory choices for dealing with a natural monopoly.
p183.zh: 那么,自然垄断的适当竞争政策是什么? 说明自然垄断的情况,市场需求曲线会削减平均成本曲线的下行部分。要点A、B、C和F说明了管理的四个主要选择。

p184.original: Regulatory Choices in Dealing with Natural Monopoly
p184.zh: 处理自然垄断的监管选择

p185.original: Regulatory Choices in Dealing with Natural Monopoly
p185.zh: 处理自然垄断的监管选择

p256.original: The first possibility is to leave the natural monopoly alone. In this case, the monopoly will follow its normal approach to maximizing profits. It determines the quantity where MR = MC, which happens at point P at a quantity of 4. The firm then looks to point A on the demand curve to find that it can charge a price of 9.3 for that profit-maximizing quantity. Since the price is above the average cost curve, the natural monopoly would earn economic profits.
p256.zh: 第一个可能性是让自然垄断独占。 在这种情况下,垄断将遵循其实现利润最大化的正常做法. 它决定MR=MC的数量,发生在P点,数量为4。 然后,该公司在需求曲线上将A点到,发现它能为利润最大化的数量收取9.3美元的价格。 由于价格高于平均成本曲线,自然垄断将赚取经济利润。

p257.original: While unlikely, a second outcome may arise if antitrust authorities decide to divide the company, so that the new firms can compete. As a simple example, imagine that the company is cut in half. Thus, instead of one large firm producing a quantity of 4, two half-size firms each produce a quantity of 2. Because of the declining average cost curve (AC), the average cost of production for each of the half-size companies producing 2, as point B shows, would be 9.75, while the average cost of production for a larger firm producing 4 would only be 7.75. Thus, the economy would become less productively efficient, since the good is produced at a higher average cost. In a situation with a downward-sloping average cost curve, two smaller firms will always have higher average costs of production than one larger firm for any quantity of total output. In addition, the antitrust authorities must worry that splitting the natural monopoly into pieces may be only the start of their problems. If one of the two firms grows larger than the other, it will have lower average costs and may be able to drive its competitor out of the market. Alternatively, two firms in a market may discover subtle ways of coordinating their behavior and keeping prices high. Either way, the result will not be the greater competition that was desired.
p257.zh: 如果反托拉斯当局决定分拆公司,以便新公司能够竞争,则可能出现第二种结果,尽管这种结果不太可能。简单来说,想象一下公司被砍成两半. 因此,一家大型公司生产4家,两家半规模公司各生产2家。 由于平均成本曲线(AC)下降,B点显示,每个生产2的半规模公司的平均生产成本为9.75,而一个生产4的大型公司的平均生产成本仅为7.75。 因此,经济的生产力效率会降低,因为商品的生产平均成本较高。 在平均成本曲线下降的情况下,两家小公司的平均生产成本将始终高于任何数量总产出的一家大公司。 此外,反托拉斯当局必须担心的是,将自然垄断分割成几块可能只是其问题的开始。 如果两家公司中的一家比另一家公司发展壮大,平均成本将较低,并可能使其竞争者退出市场。 或者,市场中的两家公司可能会发现协调其行为和保持高价格的微妙方法。 无论哪种方式,结果都不会是所期望的更大的竞争.

p258.original: A third alternative is that regulators may decide to set prices and quantities produced for this industry. The regulators will try to choose a point along the market demand curve that benefits both consumers and the broader social interest. Point C illustrates one tempting choice: the regulator requires that the firm produce the quantity of output where marginal cost crosses the demand curve at an output of 8, and charge the price of 3.5, which is equal to marginal cost at that point. This rule is appealing because it requires price to be set equal to marginal cost, which is what would occur in a perfectly competitive market, and it would assure consumers a higher quantity and lower price than at the monopoly choice A. In fact, efficient allocation of resources would occur at point C, since the value to the consumers of the last unit bought and sold in this market is equal to the marginal cost of producing it.
p258.zh: 第三种选择是,监管机构可以决定确定该行业的价格和生产数量。监管者将努力沿着市场需求曲线选择一个既有利于消费者又有利于更广泛的社会利益的点。C点说明了一种诱人的选择:监管者要求企业在边际成本超过需求曲线时以8输出量生产产出量,并收取3.5的价格,这相当于当时的边际成本. 这一规则具有吸引力,因为它要求确定价格等于边际成本,这是在完全竞争的市场中会发生的情况,它能保证消费者比垄断选择A的价格要高和低。 事实上,在C点将有效分配资源,因为在这个市场上买卖的最后一个单位对消费者的价值等于生产该单位的边际成本。

p259.original: Attempting to bring about point C through force of regulation, however, runs into a severe difficulty. At point C, with an output of 8, a price of 3.5 is below the average cost of production, which is 5.7, so if the firm charges a price of 3.5, it will be suffering losses. Unless the regulators or the government offer the firm an ongoing public subsidy (and there are numerous political problems with that option), the firm will lose money and go out of business.
p259.zh: 然而,试图通过强制管理达到C点,遇到了严重的困难。C点,产值为8,3.5的价格低于平均生产成本,5.7,因此如果企业收取3.5的价格,将遭受损失. 除非监管者或政府向公司提供持续的公共补贴(而且这一选择存在许多政治问题),否则公司将失去资金并退出业务。

p260.original: Perhaps the most plausible option for the regulator is point F; that is, to set the price where AC crosses the demand curve at an output of 6 and a price of 6.5. This plan makes some sense at an intuitive level: let the natural monopoly charge enough to cover its average costs and earn a normal rate of profit, so that it can continue operating, but prevent the firm from raising prices and earning abnormally high monopoly profits, as it would at the monopoly choice A. Determining this level of output and price with the political pressures, time constraints, and limited information of the real world is much harder than identifying the point on a graph. For more on the problems that can arise from a centrally determined price, see the discussion of price floors and price ceilings in Demand and Supply.
p260.zh: 也许监管者最可行的选择是F点,即将空调超过需求曲线的价格设定为6,价格为6.5。 这个计划在直觉上有些道理:让自然垄断费足以弥补其平均成本,并赚取正常利润率,这样它就可以继续经营,但防止公司抬高价格,赚取异常高的垄断利润,就像它选择垄断A那样.以政治压力、时间限制和现实世界有限的信息确定这一产出和价格水平比在图表上确定问题要困难得多。 关于中央确定的价格可能引起的问题,请参看关于“供求”中的价格底价和最高限价的讨论。

p262.original: Regulators of public utilities for many decades followed the general approach of attempting to choose a point like F in . They calculated the average cost of production for the water or electricity companies, added in an amount for the normal rate of profit the firm should expect to earn, and set the price for consumers accordingly. This method was known as cost-plus regulation.
p262.zh: 几十年来,公共事业的监管者遵循了试图在......中选择类似F的点的一般做法。 他们计算了水或电力公司的平均生产成本,加上了该公司预期赚取的正常利润率,并据此确定消费者的价格。这种方法被称为成本加监管。

p263.original: Cost-plus regulation raises difficulties of its own. If producers receive reimbursement for their costs, plus a bit more, then at a minimum, producers have less reason to be concerned with high costs—because they can just pass them along in higher prices. Worse, firms under cost-plus regulation even have an incentive to generate high costs by building huge factories or employing many staff, because what they can charge is linked to the costs they incur.
p263.zh: 成本加监管本身就会产生困难。 如果生产者得到成本的偿还,再加上一点,那么,至少生产者对高成本的关心就较少了,因为他们可以以更高的价格将成本转移。更糟糕的是,在成本加监管下的公司甚至有通过建造庞大的工厂或雇用许多工作人员来创造高成本的动机,因为他们能够收取的费用与其所付出的费用有关。

p264.original: Thus, in the 1980s and 1990s, some public utility regulators began to use price cap regulation, where the regulator sets a price that the firm can charge over the next few years. A common pattern was to require a price that declined slightly over time. If the firm can find ways of reducing its costs more quickly than the price caps, it can make a high level of profits. However, if the firm cannot keep up with the price caps or suffers bad luck in the market, it may suffer losses. A few years down the road, the regulators will then set a new series of price caps based on the firm’s performance.
p264.zh: 因此,在1980年代和1990年代,一些公用事业监管机构开始采用价格上限监管,监管机构在此设定公司在未来几年内可以收取的价格.一种常见的规律是,价格需要一段时间后略有下降。 如果公司能够比价格上限更快地找到降低成本的方法,那么它就可以产生高水平的利润. 但是,如果公司无法跟上价格上限或在市场上遭受厄运,它可能会遭受损失。几年之后,监管者将根据公司的业绩确定新的一系列价格上限。

p265.original: Price cap regulation requires delicacy. It will not work if the price regulators set the price cap unrealistically low. It may not work if the market changes dramatically so that the firm is doomed to incurring losses no matter what it does—say, if energy prices rise dramatically on world markets, then the company selling natural gas or heating oil to homes may not be able to meet price caps that seemed reasonable a year or two ago. However, if the regulators compare the prices with producers of the same good in other areas, they can, in effect, pressure a natural monopoly in one area to compete with the prices charged in other areas. Moreover, the possibility of earning greater profits or experiencing losses—instead of having an average rate of profit locked in every year by cost-plus regulation—can provide the natural monopoly with incentives for efficiency and innovation.
p265.zh: 价格上限管理要求精致。 如果价格监管机构不切实际地设定价格上限,那就行不通。 如果市场发生巨大变化,使公司不管做什么都注定要遭受损失,那么,如果能源价格在世界市场上急剧上涨,那么向家庭出售天然气或供暖石油的公司可能无法达到一年或两年前似乎合理的价格上限,那就可能行不通。 然而,如果监管机构将价格与其他领域同类商品的生产商进行比较,它们实际上可以迫使一个领域的自然垄断与其他地区收取的价格竞争。 此外,赚取更大利润或遭受损失的可能性——而不是每年平均利润率受到成本加条例的约束——可以为自然垄断提供提高效率和创新的动力。

p266.original: With natural monopoly, market competition is unlikely to take root, so if consumers are not to suffer the high prices and restricted output of an unrestricted monopoly, government regulation will need to play a role. In attempting to design a system of price cap regulation with flexibility and incentive, government regulators do not have an easy task.
p266.zh: 随着自然垄断,市场竞争不太可能扎根,因此,如果消费者不遭受高价和无限制垄断限制的产出,政府监管就必须发挥作用。 在试图以灵活和激励的方式设计价格上限监管制度时,政府监管者并非易事。

p268.original: In the case of a natural monopoly, market competition will not work well and so, rather than allowing an unregulated monopoly to raise price and reduce output, the government may wish to regulate price and/or output. Common examples of regulation are public utilities, the regulated firms that often provide electricity and water service.
p268.zh: 就自然垄断而言,市场竞争不会良好,因此,政府可能希望对价格和/或产出加以管制,而不是允许不受管制的垄断来提高价格和减少产出。监管的常见例子是公用事业,即经常提供水电服务的受监管公司。

p269.original: Cost-plus regulation refers to government regulating a firm which sets the price that a firm can charge over a period of time by looking at the firm’s accounting costs and then adding a normal rate of profit. Price cap regulation refers to government regulation of a firm where the government sets a price level several years in advance. In this case, the firm can either earn high profits if it manages to produce at lower costs or sell a higher quantity than expected or suffer low profits or losses if costs are high or it sells less than expected.
p269.zh: 成本加监管是指政府监管一家公司,它通过查看公司的会计成本,然后增加正常利润率,确定公司在一段时间内可以收取的价格。价格上限监管,是指政府提前数年确定价格水平的企业的政府监管. 在这种情况下,如果公司设法以较低的成本生产,或销售数量高于预期,或如果成本高或销售额低于预期,则公司可以赚取高利润,或遭受低利润或损失。

p271.original: Urban transit systems, especially those with rail systems, typically experience significant economies of scale in operation. Consider the transit system data in . Note that the quantity is in millions of riders.
p271.zh: 城市过境系统,特别是那些有铁路系统的系统,通常在运营中经历了巨大的规模经济。考虑 . 中的过境系统数据。注意数量以百万骑手为单位.

p332.original: Draw the demand, marginal revenue, marginal cost, and average cost curves. Do they have the normal shapes?
p332.zh: 绘制需求,边际收入,边际成本,以及平均成本曲线. 他们有正常的形状吗?

p333.original: Yes, all curves have normal shapes.
p333.zh: 是的,所有的曲线都有正常的形状.

p334.original: From the graph you drew to answer , would you say this transit system is a natural monopoly? Justify.
p334.zh: 从你所绘制的图表来回答, 你会说这个过境系统是天然的垄断吗?说明理由。

p335.original: Yes it is a natural monopoly because average costs decline over the range that satisfies the market demand. For example, at the point where the demand curve and the average cost curve meet, there are economies of scale.
p335.zh: 是的,这是自然垄断,因为平均成本在满足市场需求的范围内下降。 例如,在需求曲线和平均成本曲线达到时,就有规模经济.

p337.original: If public utilities are a natural monopoly, what would be the danger in deregulating them?
p337.zh: 如果公用事业属于自然垄断,那么解除对公用事业的管制有什么危险?

p338.original: If public utilities are a natural monopoly, what would be the danger in splitting them into a number of separate competing firms?
p338.zh: 如果公用事业属于自然垄断,将它们分成若干不同的竞争公司有什么危险?

p342.original: In the middle of the twentieth century, major U.S. cities had multiple competing city bus companies. Today, there is usually only one and it runs as a subsidized, regulated monopoly. What do you suppose caused the change?
p342.zh: 20世纪中叶,美国各大城市拥有多个相互竞争的城市巴士公司. 今天,通常只有一个,它是一种补贴的、有管理的垄断。 你觉得是什么导致的改变?

p343.original: Why are urban areas willing to subsidize urban transit systems? Does the argument for subsidies make sense to you?
p343.zh: 为什么城市地区愿意补贴城市交通系统?补贴的论点对你们有道理吗?

p345.original: Use  to answer the following questions.

p346.original: If the transit system were allowed to operate as an unregulated monopoly, what output would it supply and what price would it charge?
p346.zh: 如果允许过境系统作为不受管制的垄断运作,它将提供何种产出和收取何种价格?

p347.original: If the transit system were regulated to operate with no subsidy (i.e., at zero economic profit), what approximate output would it supply and what approximate price would it charge?
p347.zh: 如果对过境制度加以管制,使其运作无补贴(即零经济利润),那么它能提供多少大约产出,收取多少大约价格?

p348.original: If the transit system were regulated to provide the most allocatively efficient quantity of output, what output would it supply and what price would it charge? What subsidy would be necessary to ensure this efficient provision of transit services?
p348.zh: 如果对过境系统加以管制,以提供分配效率最高的产出数量,它将提供何种产出以及收取何种价格? 为确保有效提供过境服务,需要哪些补贴?

p350.original: Governments at all levels across the United States have regulated prices in a wide range of industries. In some cases, like water and electricity that have natural monopoly characteristics, there is some room in economic theory for such regulation. However, once politicians are given a basis to intervene in markets and to choose prices and quantities, it is hard to know where to stop.
p350.zh: 美国各级政府对各种行业的物价进行了调控.在某些情况下,像具有自然垄断特征的水和电力一样,经济理论中也有一定余地进行这种管制。 然而,一旦政治家们得到干预市场和选择价格和数量的依据,就很难知道在哪里可以停止。

p351.original: Doubts about Regulation of Prices and Quantities
p351.zh: 对价格和数量管制的怀疑

p352.original: Beginning in the 1970s, it became clear to policymakers of all political leanings that the existing price regulation was not working well. The United States carried out a great policy experiment—the deregulation that we discussed in Monopoly—removing government controls over prices and quantities produced in airlines, railroads, trucking, intercity bus travel, natural gas, and bank interest rates. The Clear It Up discusses the outcome of deregulation in one industry in particular—airlines.
p352.zh: 从1970年代开始,决策者就清楚地看到,所有政治倾向都表明,现行价格条例运作不好。 美国进行了一项伟大的政策试验——我们在垄断中讨论的放松管制——取消了政府对航空公司、铁路、卡车、城际巴士旅行、天然气和银行利率的价格和数量的控制。 《澄清报告》讨论了一个行业,特别是航空公司放松管制的结果。

p353.original: What are the results of airline deregulation?
p353.zh: 航空公司放松管制的结果如何?

p354.original: Why did the pendulum swing in favor of deregulation? Consider the airline industry. In the early days of air travel, no airline could make a profit just by flying passengers. Airlines needed something else to carry and the Postal Service provided that something with airmail. Thus, the first U.S. government regulation of the airline industry happened through the Postal Service, when in 1926 the Postmaster General began giving airlines permission to fly certain routes based on mail delivery needs—and the airlines took some passengers along for the ride. In 1934, the antitrust authorities charged the Postmaster General with colluding with the major airlines of that day to monopolize the nation’s airways. In 1938, the U.S. government created the Civil Aeronautics Board (CAB) to regulate airfares and routes instead. For 40 years, from 1938 to 1978, the CAB approved all fares, controlled all entry and exit, and specified which airlines could fly which routes. There was zero entry of new airlines on the main routes across the country for 40 years, because the CAB did not think it was necessary.
p354.zh: 为什么笔鼓会支持放松管制?想想航空业吧 在空中旅行初期,没有一家航空公司能够仅仅靠飞行乘客来赚钱.航空公司需要携带其他物品,邮政局提供带有航空邮件的物品。 因此,美国政府对航空业的第一项监管是通过邮政局发生的,1926年邮政总公司开始允许航空公司根据邮件发送需要驾驶某些航线,航空公司也带一些乘客搭乘。1934年,反托拉斯当局指控邮政总公司与当日各大航空公司串通,垄断全国的航空道.1938年,美国政府创立了民航局(CAB),以监管机票和航线代替. 从1938年到1978年的40年间,CAB批准了所有票价,控制了所有出入境,并具体规定了哪家航空公司可以飞哪条航线.40年来,全国主要航线上的新航空公司没有进入,因为行预咨委会认为没有必要。

p355.original: In 1978, the Airline Deregulation Act took the government out of the business of determining airfares and schedules. The new law shook up the industry. Famous old airlines like Pan American, Eastern, and Braniff went bankrupt and disappeared. Some new airlines like People Express were created—and then vanished.
p355.zh: 1978年,"航空公司解除管制法"使政府不再从事确定机票和时间表的业务. 新法震动了产业.泛美,东方,布兰尼夫等著名老航空公司破产后消失. 一些新航空公司,如People Express公司,被创立,然后消失。

p356.original: The greater competition from deregulation reduced airfares by about one-third over the next two decades, saving consumers billions of dollars a year. The average flight used to take off with just half its seats full; now it is two-thirds full, which is far more efficient. Airlines have also developed hub-and-spoke systems, where planes all fly into a central hub city at a certain time and then depart. As a result, one can fly between any of the spoke cities with just one connection—and there is greater service to more cities than before deregulation. With lower fares and more service, the number of air passengers doubled from the late 1970s to the start of the 2000s—an increase that, in turn, doubled the number of jobs in the airline industry. Meanwhile, with the watchful oversight of government safety inspectors, commercial air travel has continued to get safer over time.
p356.zh: 放松管制带来的竞争越大,今后20年的机票价格就越少,减少了约三分之一,每年可节省消费者数十亿美元。平均飞行通常只用一半的座位就起飞;现在只有三分之二的座位,效率要高得多。航空公司还开发了枢纽式和点名式系统,飞机在一定时间全部飞入中心枢纽城市,然后离开.如此一来,人们就可以在任何仅有一种联系的有发言权的城市之间飞行,而且对更多城市的服务也比放松管制之前更大。 由于票价较低而且服务较多,从1970年代末到2000年代初,航空旅客人数翻了一番——这一增加又使航空业的就业机会翻了一番。 与此同时,在政府安全检查员的严密监督下,商业航空旅行随着时间的推移继续变得更加安全。

p357.original: The U.S. airline industry is far from perfect.  For example, a string of mergers in recent years has raised concerns over how competition might be compromised.
p357.zh: 美国航空业远非完美. 例如,近年来一连串的合并引起了人们对如何损害竞争的关切。

p358.original: One difficulty with government price regulation is what economists call regulatory capture, in which the firms that are supposedly regulated end up playing a large role in setting the regulations that they will follow. When the airline industry was regulated, for example, it suggested appointees to the regulatory board, sent lobbyists to argue with the board, provided most of the information on which the board made decisions, and offered well-paid jobs to at least some of the people leaving the board. In this situation, it is easy for regulators to poorly represent consumers. The result of regulatory capture is that government price regulation can often become a way for existing competitors to work together to reduce output, keep prices high, and limit competition.
p358.zh: 政府价格监管的一个困难是经济学家所谓的监管捕捉,在这种捕捉中,据称受监管的公司最终在制定它们将遵循的监管方面发挥很大作用。 例如,当航空业受到管制时,它建议由管理委员会任命,派游说者与董事会辩论,提供董事会作出决定所依据的大部分信息,并向至少离开董事会的一些人提供高薪工作。 在这种情况下,监管者很容易不适当地代表消费者。监管捕捉的结果是,政府价格监管常常会成为现有竞争者共同努力减少产出,保持价格高位,限制竞争的一种方式.

p360.original: Deregulation, both of airlines and of other industries, has its negatives. The greater pressure of competition led to entry and exit. When firms went bankrupt or contracted substantially in size, they laid off workers who had to find other jobs. Market competition is, after all, a full-contact sport.
p360.zh: 航空公司和其他行业的放松管制都有其负面作用。竞争压力的加大导致了出入境. 当企业破产或规模大到要裁员时,就会解雇那些不得不找到其他工作的工人。市场竞争毕竟是全接触运动.

p361.original: A number of major accounting scandals involving prominent corporations such as Enron, Tyco International, and WorldCom led to the Sarbanes-Oxley Act in 2002. The government designed Sarbanes-Oxley to increase confidence in financial information provided by public corporations to protect investors from accounting fraud.
p361.zh: 涉及安然公司,泰科国际公司,世界通信公司等知名公司的一些重大会计丑闻导致2002年的"萨班斯-奥克斯利法案". 政府设计了Sarbanes-Oxley,以提高对公营公司提供的财务信息的信心,保护投资者免遭会计欺诈。

p362.original: The Great Recession, which began in late 2007, was caused at least in part by a global financial crisis, which began in the United States. The key component of the crisis was the creation and subsequent failure of several types of unregulated financial assets, such as collateralized mortgage obligations (CMOs, a type of mortgage-backed security), and credit default swaps (CDSs, insurance contracts on assets like CMOs that provided a payoff even if the holder of the CDS did not own the CMO). Private credit rating agencies such as Standard & Poors, Moody’s, and Fitch rated many of these assets very safe.
p362.zh: 2007年末开始的大衰退至少部分是由于始于美国的全球金融危机.危机的关键组成部分是,几类不受管制的金融资产的产生和随后的失败,如抵押抵押债务(CMO,一种抵押担保)和信用违约互换(CDS,对像CMO这样的资产提供的保险合同,即使CDS的持有人并不拥有CMO).私人信用评级机构,如标准普尔公司、穆迪公司和Fitch公司,对其中许多资产评为非常安全。

p363.original: The collapse of the markets for these assets precipitated the financial crisis and led to the failure of Lehman Brothers, a major investment bank, numerous large commercial banks, such as Wachovia, and even the Federal National Mortgage Corporation (Fannie Mae), which had to be nationalized—that is, taken over by the federal government. One response to the financial crisis was the Dodd-Frank Act, which majorly attempted to reform the financial system. The legislation’s purpose, as noted on dodd-frank.com is:
p363.zh: 这些资产的市场崩溃引发了金融危机,并导致主要投资银行莱曼兄弟公司、瓦乔维亚等众多大型商业银行以及甚至联邦国家抵押公司(Fannie Mae)的失败,后者必须国有化,即由联邦政府接管。应对金融危机的一个对策是《多德-弗兰克法案》,它主要试图改革金融制度。 如dodd-frank.com所述,立法的目的是:

p364.original: To promote the financial stability of the United States by improving accountability and transparency in the financial system, to end “too big to fail,” to protect the American taxpayer by ending bailouts, [and] to protect consumers from abusive financial services practices. . .
p364.zh: 通过加强金融体系的问责制和透明度,促进美国金融稳定,结束“太大到不能失败”,通过结束救助来保护美国纳税人,[ 保护消费者免受滥用金融服务的做法。

p365.original: All market-based economies operate against a background of laws and regulations, including laws about enforcing contracts, collecting taxes, and protecting health and the environment. The government policies that we discussed in this chapter—like blocking certain anticompetitive mergers, ending restrictive practices, imposing price cap regulation on natural monopolies, and deregulation—demonstrate the role of government to strengthen the incentives that come with a greater degree of competition.
p365.zh: 所有市场经济都以法律和规章为背景,包括关于执行合同、征税和保护健康和环境的法律。 我们本章所讨论的政府政策,如阻止某些反竞争的兼并,结束限制性做法,对自然垄断实行价格上限管制,以及放松管制等,表明政府的作用,以加强竞争程度更高的奖励措施。

p367.original: What did the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) decide on the Kinder Morgan / El Paso Corporation merger? After careful examination, federal officials decided there was only one area of significant overlap that might provide the merged firm with strong market power. The FTC approved the merger, provided Kinder Morgan divest itself of the overlap area. Tallgrass purchased Kinder Morgan Interstate Gas Transmission, Trailblazer Pipeline Co. LLC, two processing facilities in Wyoming, and Kinder Morgan’s 50 percent interest in the Rockies Express Pipeline to meet the FTC requirements. The FTC was attempting to strike a balance between potential cost reductions resulting from economies of scale and concentration of market power.
p367.zh: 联邦贸易委员会(FTC)对Kinder Morgan / El Paso公司合并的决定是什么? 经过仔细审查,联邦官员决定只有一个领域存在重大重叠,可能使合并后的公司拥有强大的市场力量.公平贸易委员会批准了合并,但Kinder Morgan必须放弃重叠领域。高草公司购买了Kinder Morgan州际天然气传输公司,Trailblazer管道公司.LLC,Wyoming的两个加工设施,以及Kinder Morgan对落基山脉快运管道的50%的利息,以满足FTC的要求.公平贸易委员会正在设法在规模经济可能减少的费用和市场力量集中之间取得平衡。

p368.original: Did the price of natural gas decrease? Yes, rather significantly. In 2010, the wellhead price of natural gas was $4.48 per thousand cubic foot. In 2012 the price had fallen to just $2.66. Was the merger responsible for the large drop in price? The answer is uncertain. The larger contributor to the sharp drop in price was the overall increase in the supply of natural gas. Increasingly, more natural gas was able to be recovered by fracturing shale deposits, a process called fracking. Fracking, which is controversial for environmental reasons, enabled the recovery of known reserves of natural gas that previously were not economically feasible to tap. Kinder Morgan’s control of 80,000-plus miles of pipeline likely made moving the gas from wellheads to end users smoother and allowed for an even greater benefit from the increased supply.
p368.zh: 天然气价格是否下降? 是的,相当重要。2010年,天然气井头价格为每千立方英尺4.48美元.2012年,价格跌至2.66美元。兼并是否造成价格大幅下跌?答案是不确定的。造成价格急剧下降的更大原因是天然气供应的总体增加。越来越多的天然气能够通过断裂页岩矿床而回收,这一过程被称为裂缝。 由于环境原因引起争议的裂缝使已知的天然气储量得以回收,而这些储量以前在经济上不可行,因此无法开采。Kinder Morgan控制着8万多英里的管道,这很可能使天然气从井口转移到终端用户,并使得供应的增加能够带来更大的利益。

p370.original: The U.S. economy experienced a wave of deregulation in the late 1970s and early 1980s, when the government eliminated a number of regulations that had set prices and quantities produced in a number of industries. Major accounting scandals in the early 2000s and, more recently, the Great Recession have spurred new regulation to prevent similar occurrences in the future. Regulatory capture occurs when the regulated industries end up having a strong influence over what regulations exist.
p370.zh: 20世纪70年代末和80年代初,美国经济经历了放松管制的浪潮,当时政府取消了一些规定一些行业的价格和生产量的法规.2000年代初期和最近大衰退期间的重大会计丑闻促使了新的条例,以防止今后发生类似事件。监管捕捉是在受监管的行业最终对存在哪些监管产生强大影响时发生的。

p373.zh: 是什么现实世界的变化使得放松管制成为可能?

p375.original: What are some of the benefits of the deregulation?

p376.original: More consumer choice. Cheaper phone calls, especially long distance. Better-quality phone service in many cases. Cheaper, faster, and better-quality data transmission. Spin-off technologies like free Internet-based calling and video calling.
p376.zh: 更多消费者的选择。便宜的电话,尤其是长途电话。在许多情况下,电话服务质量更高。更便宜,更快,质量更好的数据传输.免费网络电话和视频电话等附带技术.

p377.original: What might some of the negatives of deregulation be?
p377.zh: 放松管制的消极因素是什么?

p378.original: More choice can sometimes make for difficult decisions—not knowing if you got the best plan for your situation, for example. Some phone service providers are less reliable than AT&T used to be.
p378.zh: 有时,更多的选择可以做出困难的决定——不知道你是否对自身情况有最佳计划。 一些电话服务提供商的可靠性不如AT&T以前.

c4.original: A natural monopoly will maximize profits by producing at the quantity where marginal revenue (MR) equals marginal costs (MC) and by then looking to the market demand curve to see what price to charge for this quantity. This monopoly will produce at point A, with a quantity of 4 and a price of 9.3. If antitrust regulators split this company exactly in half, then each half would produce at point B, with average costs of 9.75 and output of 2. The regulators might require the firm to produce where marginal cost crosses the market demand curve at point C. However, if the firm is required to produce at a quantity of 8 and sell at a price of 3.5, the firm will incur losses. The most likely choice is point F, where the firm is required to produce a quantity of 6 and charge a price of 6.5.
c4.zh: 自然垄断将实现利润最大化,办法是在边际收入等于边际成本(MC)时生产数量,然后看看市场需求曲线,看看对这一数量收取什么价格。 这种垄断将在A点产生,数量为4,价格为9.3。 如果反托拉斯监管机构将这家公司完全分成一半,那么每半半个公司将在B点生产,平均成本为9.75美元,产出为2.监管机构可能要求公司在边际成本超过C点市场需求曲线的地方生产。 但是,如果要求公司以8个数量生产,并以3.5个价格出售,则公司将蒙受损失。 最可能的选择是F点,即要求公司生产6个数量并收取6.5美元的价格。
